data.narrative:
Space42, a publicly listed Space & Aerospace company formed through the merger of Bayanat and Yahsat, has raised $695M+ in ECA financing. The valuation universe comprises 11 same-sector peers: 5 public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space.

Standard triangulation methods face material constraints. Peer-median multiples are inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables—while 11 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy simultaneous filters for stage, operational tier, and valuation proximity, falling below the minimum three-datapoint threshold. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot proceed because target revenue is not disclosed; the broader Space & Aerospace sector median P/S stands at 23.9x across the 6 public tickers, but applying this multiple requires known revenue. Neither method yields a defensible result.

The analysis cannot support a specific valuation range without either (1) target revenue figures for P/S application, (2) EBITDA or adjusted earnings for comparable-multiple bridging, or (3) strategic transaction precedents within the narrow merger-and-acquisition subset. Key uncertainties include the operational and financial metrics underpinning the Bayanat–Yahsat combination, segment revenue splits, and whether comparable private valuations (SpaceX, Sierra Space) reflect comparable stages of development or capital intensity. A complete valuation requires disclosure of audited or internally-verified financial metrics.
